gloss: to take the plunge, to make a decision

definitions.gloss: to take the plunge, to make a decisive move
definitions.explanation: To make a firm decision to do something significant, especially after hesitation.
To push off the ground with one's foot to jump or leap, as in athletics.

examples.japanese: ついに{転職|てんしょく}に{踏|ふ}み{切|き}った。
examples.english: I finally took the plunge and changed jobs.

examples.japanese: {起業|きぎょう}に{踏|ふ}み{切|き}るには{勇気|ゆうき}がいる。
examples.english: It takes courage to take the plunge into starting a business.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}{悩|なや}んだ{末|すえ}、{海外|かいがい}{移住|いじゅう}に{踏|ふ}み{切|き}ることにした。
examples.english: After years of deliberation, I decided to take the plunge and move abroad.

examples.japanese: {左足|ひだりあし}で{踏|ふ}み{切|き}って{跳|と}んだ。
examples.english: I pushed off with my left foot and jumped.

examples.japanese: {選手|せんしゅ}は{力強|ちからづよ}く{踏|ふ}み{切|き}って{跳|と}んだ。
examples.english: The athlete pushed off powerfully and jumped.

examples.japanese: {踏|ふ}み{切|き}る{位置|いち}がずれて、ファウルになってしまった。
examples.english: The takeoff position was off, and it ended up being a foul.

notes:
USAGE: {踏|ふ}み{切|き}る is a compound verb combining {踏|ふ}む (to step on) and {切|き}る (to cut, completion). The figurative sense (sense 1) of making a decisive commitment is more common in everyday use.

TRANSITIVITY: Intransitive ({自動詞|じどうし}). Takes に for the action one decides to take.

ASPECT: {踏|ふ}み{切|き}った emphasizes completion of the decision. {踏|ふ}み{切|き}れない indicates inability to make the decision.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{決断|けつだん}に{踏|ふ}み{切|き}る (to make a firm decision)
・{購入|こうにゅう}に{踏|ふ}み{切|き}る (to take the plunge to purchase)
・{独立|どくりつ}に{踏|ふ}み{切|き}る (to decide to become independent)

RELATED: {踏切|ふみきり} (railroad crossing) uses the same kanji but is a different word.

NOTE: Often used with ついに or {思|おも}い{切|き}って to emphasize the decisiveness.
